blockers.title: Raw forbidden-name absence is not an executable kexec-capability proof
evidence: kexecSymbolAbsence scans decompressed payload P only for eleven contiguous UTF-8 spellings. It does not parse a symbol table, prove such a table is present and complete, inspect syscall or operation dispatch entries, disassemble reachable code, or relate any matching or absent byte sequence to executable semantics.

C identifiers are not required runtime data. Machine code dispatches by addresses, not by its source-level function names. A build with CONFIG_KALLSYMS=n can retain the kexec syscall and implementation while omitting the names; a build with compressed kallsyms need not contain any full name contiguously; a semantically identical implementation can also use wrapper-local or renamed symbols outside the closed list.

The claimed Claude route (2) asked for an independently verifiable code-capability proof and gave named symbols or their dispatch-table entries as an example. v39 implements only a raw-byte name scan. It neither proves the listed names are exhaustive nor checks dispatch entries, so calling the haystack executable content does not make name absence a property of the code.

Concrete intended-passing counterexample: an authenticated measured kernel K is built with CONFIG_KEXEC=y, CONFIG_KALLSYMS=n, CONFIG_IKCONFIG=n, and without the optional sysctl node. No kexec image is initially loaded. K's P contains none of the eleven strings, the optional IKCONFIG branch is absent, the present-state checks do not refuse, and the signed result agrees. The contract returns kexec-absent even though K can later load and execute an undeclared kernel M.

Exact member sha256, Authenticode digest, PCR event binding, and signed result equality authenticate K and the false derived token; they do not turn absent labels into absent functionality. The false result therefore survives every downstream join.
blockers.impact: A kexec-capable exact measured kernel can qualify as kexec-absent and replace itself with undeclared OS-ABI code. The positive PATHLESS attestation is false and the platform TCB remains open.
blockers.requiredRepair: Replace raw-name scanning with a reproducible proof over executable capability: for example a version-pinned complete symbol-and-dispatch analysis with a specified completeness predicate and control-flow relation, independently authenticated builder provenance binding the exact executable to the exact disabling build inputs, or measured runtime enforcement that makes replacement impossible. Add CONFIG_KALLSYMS=n, compressed-kallsyms, renamed-wrapper, and dispatch-entry counterexamples whose code retains kexec while every forbidden string is absent.

blockers.title: The PE entry path still is not proven to consume the selected payload
evidence: The official fixed x86 offsets and the tightened arm64 header rules make selection of a range deterministic. Machine, entry-point-section, and loaded-range checks remain generic PE layout predicates and do not prove that the entry path transfers control to or consumes that selected range.

peJoin.notInert labels itself OPERATION but its actual operation is only selection of the unique official range. Its final sentence says a wrapper that would require a different payload refuses without defining a parser, call/relocation relation, canonical stub identity, observer, signed predicate, or payload measurement by which a verifier detects that condition.

The entryPoint rule only requires AddressOfEntryPoint inside some loaded executable section. loadedRange permits the selected range in one or more loaded sections. Neither requires reachability from the entry point or even that the selected bytes be interpreted as the launched kernel.

Concrete counterexample: an authenticated measured PE has entry section T that boots kexec-capable kernel K. A separate loaded section Q carries a valid official-header-selected safe-looking payload P. FileHeader.Machine matches, the entry point is executable, Q is loaded, all offsets and bounds pass, P lacks the forbidden names, and all signed hashes/results agree. Only the unevaluable conclusion that T consumes P would reject the wrapper.

The same gap survives the arm64 repair: a loaded section can satisfy unique zimg or the 0x38 ARMd test while entry section T ignores it. Exact wrapper authentication proves which wrapper ran, not which internal range that wrapper consumed.
blockers.impact: An exactly authenticated wrapper can qualify from safe loaded bytes that are not the executed kernel. The kexec result can therefore describe inert data while a different kexec-capable kernel executes.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define a reproducible, version-pinned entry-to-payload proof, such as a canonical EFI-stub identity plus exact header/relocation/control-transfer relation, an independently signed builder predicate covering that relation, or direct measurement of the decompressed executed payload. Add x86 and arm64 loaded-section decoys whose entry points ignore the selected range.

shouldFix.title: The closed succession roster omits a changed authenticated-kernel clause
evidence: A duplicate-key-free recursive semantic diff from v38 to v39 finds 47 changed leaves and exactly one outside the closed roster: /loaderTraces/objectAuthenticityBind/tags/linux-pathless/authenticatedKernelMember.

v38 required a mandatory ikconfigDigest and generic equality to kexecAbsenceDerivation.result. v39 changes that clause to optional ikconfigDigest and explicit result projections. That is a normative change, not a byte-only formatting difference.

basedOn.method rosters measuredBootBind.kexecAbsenceDerivation, which is a sibling rather than an ancestor of authenticatedKernelMember. No other roster entry contains it, so the declaration that every unrostered path is unchanged is false.
shouldFix.impact: The successor cannot be reproduced under its own closed-change discipline; a reviewer following the roster can miss a normative authenticity-shape change.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Add the exact authenticatedKernelMember path, or a deliberate containing ancestor, to the closed roster and reissue the successor with a truthful semantic-diff statement.

shouldFix.title: IKCONFIG and build provenance are simultaneously optional and mandatory
evidence: ikconfig.ifPresent and result define a successful absent-IKCONFIG branch: absence does not refuse and result.ikconfigDigest is absent. The earlier governing ikconfigPair clause still requires exactly one pair and says zero pairs refuse; extract and kconfigSerialization are likewise unconditional.

signedObject.linuxForm includes ikconfigDigest only when result.ikconfigDigest is present, while the signedObject.ikconfigDigest field says it is required on every Linux OS ABI entry. fromBootLockdown.signedCarriage also unconditionally requires signedObject.ikconfigDigest to equal a derived digest.

buildProvenance is optional, but kconfigSerialization.utsRelease unconditionally dereferences signedObject.buildProvenance.kernelRelease. Its closed record also always contains ikconfigDigest even though the result digest may be absent and only defines fieldwise equality when both are present.

Consequently the exact stripped-kernel branch central to PTCB-V39-B1 is either accepted by the new optional rule or rejected by the retained mandatory rule. Both readings are literal and no precedence sentence chooses one.
shouldFix.impact: Conforming validators can disagree whether an IKCONFIG-free or provenance-free kernel qualifies, and the purported absent branch has no single executable closed-form interpretation.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define explicit present and absent branches, state their precedence, and propagate them consistently through marker cardinality, extraction, serialization, result, authenticatedKernelMember, signedObject, buildProvenance, fromBootLockdown, refusals, and negative tests. Remove every unconditional dereference on an absent branch.

shouldFix.title: Stale result paths and the G22 claim contradict the v39 proof model
evidence: signedObject.kexecCapability still says the scalar token MUST equal generic 'the derivation output' rather than result.kexecCapability. The derivation output is now described as result.kexecCapability plus optional result.ikconfigDigest, so this retained equality revives the scalar-to-record ambiguity.
signedObject.ikconfigDigest still targets kexecAbsenceDerivation.ikconfigDigest, a path that does not exist in the v39 derivation. The defined field is kexecAbsenceDerivation.result.ikconfigDigest.

g22.doesNotClaim still states that kexec-absent is derived from authenticated-member IKCONFIG. v39 instead declares IKCONFIG corroboration only and kexecSymbolAbsence the structural proof. The qualification-evidence description therefore names a different proof authority than the contract.

honestyRepairsFromV38 claims every equality names result.kexecCapability or result.ikconfigDigest and never generic derivation output. The two retained signedObject clauses directly disprove that honesty claim.
shouldFix.impact: The contract has conflicting proof authorities and result joins, allowing validators and the reserved G22 evidence to implement different governing semantics.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Replace every generic or obsolete equality with the exact result projection, and rewrite G22 and honestyRepairsFromV38 to name the actual v39 proof authority and only repairs that the final text truly contains.
